title: Proprietary Costs and Corporate Lobbying Against Changes in Mandatory Disclosure
eligible_reason: SFAS 131 is a single mandate effective for fiscal years beginning after 15 Dec 1997; in LobbyingFirm_panel.dta the adoption year (adoption == 0) is fyear 1998 for 105 firms and fyear 1999 for 17 firms, i.e. calendar timing differs only by fiscal-year end, with fyear FE. Under the PROTOCOL 6 ruling for mnsc.2022.4515 this is a single-policy design, not staggered adoption. The treatment is chg x post (segment-changing lobbying firms vs non-changing firms that also adopt), and every reported column also includes time-varying controls (size, leverage, con4, avginv, beta, sale_growth); Tables 5-7 part 2 add robust-regression (robreg mm) weights.
design_notes: Firm-year panel 1992-2000 of 122 firms that lobbied against SFAS 131 (77 change firms, 45 non-change). Table 4: reghdfe roa on chg x pre/post event indicators + controls, absorb(gvkey fyear), cluster sic2. Table 5 Panels C-D: non-lobbying firms by lobbying-industry indicator with robreg weights. Tables 6-7: chg_large_post / chg_small_post intensity split; sales growth, margin, turnover outcomes. Table 2: probit of lobbying.
estimators_reported: twfe event study (pre/post bins) with controls
n_adoption_cohorts: 2 fiscal-year cohorts (1998, 1999) of one mandate; not counted as staggered

specs.exclusion_reason: single mandate with timing differing only by fiscal-year end (single-policy design); time-varying controls in every column
single-policy design; time-varying controls; robreg mm weights

data_provenance_note: Compustat-derived firm-year panels and hand-collected lobbying data shipped as .dta.
screener_notes: Fails on design (single-mandate, fiscal-year-end timing, as mnsc.2022.4515), so not a near-miss even though controls are the other violation. Screened from package only.
